title: Rabbi Ada (or Rabbi Ida) of Caesarea
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places Rabbi Ada of Caesarea among the third-generation Amoraim of the Land of Israel and identifies him as a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In [Moed Katan 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.20b.4) he recites a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan. He reports in Rabbi Yochanan’s name at [the end of chapter 4 of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.4.6.7), in [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.4.3), and again at [the end of Rosh Hashanah](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.10.5).

notes.text: In Moed Katan, Rabbi Ada recites a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan about news of a death that arrives on Shabbat. In the linked Yerushalmi passages Rabbi Ada transmits rulings in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.

[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=215&lang=en) cites the recitation and the end of Berakhot 4 and Rosh Hashanah. His notice also discusses a possible reading with “the Elder” in Moed Katan and a name variant involving Abba of Caesarea.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 105) gives Ida as an alternative in the heading and reads “the end of Rosh Hashanah” (סוף ר״ה), where the supplied transcription has סוף א״ה. Rosh Hashanah 4:10:5 parallels the report at the end of Berakhot chapter 4. The classification by generation is Hyman’s.
